message.content: We need per-API-key rate limiting for the public endpoints. Sliding window or token bucket?

content.text: Token bucket. It allows short bursts (which real clients produce) while capping the sustained rate, and it is O(1) per request: refill lazily from the elapsed time, decrement on use. Sliding window counters are cheaper but punish bursty-but-legitimate clients.

Redis with a small Lua script so the read-refill-write is atomic. Store per key: token count and last-refill timestamp. Set the bucket capacity to the burst you want to tolerate and the refill rate to the sustained limit.
